STATEMENT OF INFORMATION (CALIFORNIA SECRETARY OF STATE PERIODIC FILING)
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

STATEMENT OF INFORMATION — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This Statement of Information relates to Acme, Inc., a California stock corporation. Filing articles of incorporation or articles of organization with the California Secretary of State creates a business entity, but it does not end that entity's reporting obligations to the state. California law separately requires the entity to periodically file a Statement of Information with the Secretary of State after formation, reporting current information such as the entity's officers, directors, managers, or members; its agent for service of process; and its principal business address, so the state's public record stays current. This is a California state filing made with the Secretary of State. It is separate from, and unrelated to, any federal reporting obligation that may apply to a business entity — including, for some entities, federal beneficial ownership reporting under the Corporate Transparency Act. This document's research addressed only the California statutes governing this state filing; it did not research or verify the current status, scope, or requirements of any federal reporting regime, which has been the subject of significant federal litigation and rulemaking changes in recent years. Any reference to a federal regime here is unverified background context, not this document's authority, and not a substitute for checking that federal requirement directly.

INITIAL AND RECURRING FILING DEADLINES
California sets separate statutory deadlines for a corporation's Statement of Information and an LLC's Statement of Information, and the two schedules are not the same. A California corporation must file an initial statement within 90 days after its articles of incorporation are filed, and then again every year during its assigned filing period. A California LLC must also file an initial statement within 90 days after its articles of organization are filed, but its recurring filing is biennial — once every two years — rather than annual. For both entity types, the assigned filing period is measured as the calendar month in which the entity's original articles were filed, together with the five calendar months immediately before it. The Secretary of State sends a reminder notice roughly three months before that period closes, but the statute itself states that not receiving that notice does not excuse a failure to comply.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "Every corporation shall file, within 90 days after the filing of its original articles and annually thereafter during the applicable filing period, on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State, a statement containing all of the following:"
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 1502(a), California General Corporation Law, initial and annual statement of information (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=1502.)
  "For the purposes of this section, the applicable filing period for a corporation shall be the calendar month during which its original articles were filed and the immediately preceding five calendar months. The Secretary of State shall provide a notice to each corporation to comply with this section approximately three months prior to the close of the applicable filing period. The notice shall state the due date for compliance and shall be sent to the last address of the corporation according to the records of the Secretary of State or to the last electronic mail address according to the records of the Secretary of State if the corporation has elected to receive notices from the Secretary of State by electronic mail. The failure of the corporation to receive the notice is not an excuse for failure to comply with this section."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 1502(d), California General Corporation Law, how the annual filing period is measured (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=1502.)
  "Every limited liability company and every foreign limited liability company registered to transact intrastate business in this state shall deliver to the Secretary of State for filing within 90 days after the filing of its original articles of organization or registering to transact intrastate business and biennially thereafter during the applicable filing period, on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State, a statement of information containing:"
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09(a), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, initial and biennial statement of information (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.09.)
  "For purposes of this section, the applicable filing period for a limited liability company shall be the calendar month during which its original articles of organization was filed or, in the case of a foreign limited liability company, the month during which its application for registration was filed, and the immediately preceding five calendar months. The Secretary of State shall provide a notice to each limited liability company or foreign limited liability company to comply with this section approximately three months prior to the close of the applicable filing period. The notice shall state the due date for compliance and shall be sent to the last mailing address of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company according to the records of the Secretary of State, or if none, to the street address of the principal office, or, in the case of a domestic limited liability company, the office required to be maintained pursuant to Section 17701.13, or to the last electronic mail address according to the records of the Secretary of State if the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company has elected to receive notices from the Secretary of State by electronic mail. The failure of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company to receive the notice shall not exempt the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company from complying with this section."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09(c), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, how the two-year filing period is measured (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.09.)

This clause cites two different statutory sections, one for each entity type: Cal. Corp. Code § 1502 (corporations) and Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09 (LLCs). Within each section, two subsections are cited together and treated as one source per section, not as independent sources: § 1502(a) and § 1502(d) are both subsections of the same corporate statute, and § 17702.09(a) and § 17702.09(c) are both subsections of the same LLC statute. The annual-versus-biennial distinction was verified directly against the current statutory text rather than assumed: § 1502(a) fixes the corporate cycle at 'annually,' and § 17702.09(a) fixes the LLC cycle at 'biennially,' in the current, currently-operative text of each section.

INFORMATION A CORPORATION'S STATEMENT MUST REPORT
For a domestic stock corporation, the statement California requires must include: the corporation's name and Secretary of State file number; the names and complete business or residence addresses of its incumbent directors, and the number of any board vacancies; the names and complete business or residence addresses of its chief executive officer, secretary, and chief financial officer; the street address of its principal executive office and, if different, its mailing address; a statement of the general type of business that constitutes the corporation's principal business activity; and a statement disclosing whether any officer or director has an outstanding, non-appealable judgment against them for violating a wage order or the Labor Code. The statement must also designate the corporation's agent for service of process — either a natural person residing in California, whose complete business or residence street address must also be listed, or a qualifying corporate agent, for whom no address is listed.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "(1) The name of the corporation and the Secretary of State’s file number. (2) The names and complete business or residence addresses of its incumbent directors. (3) The number of vacancies on the board, if any. (4) The names and complete business or residence addresses of its chief executive officer, secretary, and chief financial officer. (5) The street address of its principal executive office. (6) The mailing address of the corporation, if different from the street address of its principal executive office. (7) If the address of its principal executive office is not in this state, the street address of its principal business office in this state, if any. (8) If the corporation chooses to receive renewal notices and any other notifications from the Secretary of State by electronic mail instead of by United States mail, the corporation shall include a valid electronic mail address for the corporation or for the corporation’s designee to receive those notices. (9) A statement of the general type of business that constitutes the principal business activity of the corporation, such as, for example, manufacturer of aircraft, wholesale liquor distributor, or retail department store. (10) A statement indicating whether any officer or any director has an outstanding final judgment issued by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement or a court of law, for which no appeal therefrom is pending, for the violation of any wage order or provision of the Labor Code."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 1502(a), California General Corporation Law, required content of the statement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=1502.)
  "The statement required by subdivision (a) shall also designate, as the agent of the corporation for the purpose of service of process, a natural person residing in this state or a corporation that has complied with Section 1505 and whose capacity to act as an agent has not terminated. If a natural person is designated, the statement shall set forth that person’s complete business or residence street address. If a corporate agent is designated, no address for it shall be set forth."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 1502(b), California General Corporation Law, agent-for-service-of-process designation rule (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=1502.)

INFORMATION AN LLC'S STATEMENT MUST REPORT
For a California LLC, the statement must include: the LLC's name and Secretary of State file number; the name and street address of its agent for service of process (if the agent is a corporate agent, only the agent's name is listed, not an address); the street address of its principal office and, if different, its mailing address; the names and complete business or residence addresses of its manager or managers and chief executive officer, if any — or, if the LLC has no manager, the name and business or residence address of each member; and a statement of the general type of business that constitutes the LLC's principal business activity. The statement must also disclose whether any manager, in a manager-managed LLC, or any member, in a member-managed LLC, has an outstanding, non-appealable judgment against them for violating a wage order or the Labor Code.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "(1) The name of the limited liability company and the Secretary of State’s file number and, in the case of a foreign limited liability company, the name under which the foreign limited liability company is authorized to transact intrastate business in this state and the state or other jurisdiction under the laws of which it is organized. (2) The name and street address of the agent in this state for service of process required to be maintained pursuant to Section 17701.13. If a corporate agent is designated, only the name of the agent shall be set forth. (3) The street address of its principal office. In the case of a foreign limited liability company, the street address of its principal business office in this state, if any, and, in the case of a domestic limited liability company, the street address of the office required to be maintained pursuant to Section 17701.13. (4) The mailing address of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company, if different from the street address of its principal office, or principal business office in this state, or, in the case of a domestic limited liability company, the street address of the office required to be maintained pursuant to Section 17701.13. (5) The name and complete business or residence addresses of any manager or managers and the chief executive officer, if any, appointed or elected in accordance with the articles of organization or operating agreement or, if no manager has been so elected or appointed, the name and business or residence address of each member. (6) If the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company chooses to receive renewal notices and any other notifications from the Secretary of State by electronic mail instead of by United States mail, the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company shall include a valid electronic mail address for the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company, or for the limited liability company’s or foreign limited liability company’s designee to receive those notices. (7) The general type of business that constitutes the principal business activity of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company, such as, for example, manufacturer of aircraft, wholesale liquor distributor, or retail department store. (8) (A) For a manager-managed limited liability company or a manager-managed foreign limited liability company, a statement indicating whether any manager has an outstanding final judgment issued by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement or a court of law, for which no appeal therefrom is pending, for the violation of any wage order or provision of the Labor Code. (B) For a member-managed limited liability company, a statement indicating whether any member has an outstanding final judgment issued by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement or a court of law, for which no appeal therefrom is pending, for the violation of any wage order or provision of the Labor Code, unless, pursuant to subdivision (d) of Section 17701.10, a written operating agreement limits the members who are agents of the limited liability company for the purpose of its business and affairs to a specified member or specified members, in which case the statement is only required with respect to the specified member or members. (C) For a foreign limited liability company that is not managed by a manager or managers, a statement indicating whether any member has an outstanding final judgment issued by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement or a court of law, for which no appeal therefrom is pending, for the violation of any wage order or provision of the Labor Code, unless the member is not an agent of the foreign limited liability company for purposes of its business and affairs, in which case the statement is only required with respect to the member or members who are agents of the foreign limited liability company."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09(a), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, required content of the statement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.09.)

THE 'NO CHANGE' ALTERNATIVE TO REFILING
When nothing reported in an entity's most recently filed statement has changed, California does not require the entity to prepare and refile a full new Statement of Information for the next filing period. Instead, both corporations and LLCs may, in lieu of refiling, advise the Secretary of State — on a form the Secretary of State prescribes — that no changes to the previously reported information have occurred during the applicable filing period.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "If there has been no change in the information in the last filed statement of the corporation on file in the Secretary of State’s office, the corporation may, in lieu of filing the statement required by subdivisions (a) and (b), advise the Secretary of State, on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State, that no changes in the required information have occurred during the applicable filing period."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 1502(c), California General Corporation Law, certifying no changes in lieu of refiling (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=1502.)
  "If there has been no change in the information contained in the last filed statement of information of the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company on file in the office of Secretary of State, the limited liability company or foreign limited liability company may, in lieu of filing the statement of information required by subdivision (a), advise the Secretary of State, on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State, that no changes in the required information have occurred during the applicable filing period."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.09(b), California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, certifying no changes in lieu of refiling (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.09.)

Each is a single subsection of its own section, so no same-section multiple-citation issue arises within either citation, though the two provisions are textually near-identical and are being used here as parallel, independently verified evidence for the two different entity types, not as one source standing in for the other.

CURRENT INFORMATION FOR THE NEXT FILING
The information below reflects Acme, Inc.'s current records for use in preparing its next Statement of Information filing with the California Secretary of State. Principal office address: 500 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105. Agent for service of process: Jordan Lee, at 500 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105. Current officers and directors (if Acme, Inc. is a corporation) or managers and members (if Acme, Inc. is an LLC): Jordan Lee, CEO; Pat Morgan, Secretary and CFO. General type of business that constitutes Acme, Inc.'s principal business activity: Software as a service for small business accounting. This worksheet organizes the entity's current information for reference. It is not itself the Secretary of State's official statement form, which must be completed and filed in the format the Secretary of State prescribes.

THE $250 PENALTY FOR A DELINQUENT FILING
Failing to file a required Statement of Information carries a specific statutory monetary penalty, separate from any Secretary of State filing fee. If a corporation or LLC does not file, the Secretary of State first sends the entity a notice of delinquency describing the penalty and the entity's right to request relief for reasonable cause or unusual circumstances that justify the failure to file. If the required statement still has not been filed 60 days after that notice, the Secretary of State certifies the entity's name to the Franchise Tax Board. Upon that certification, the Franchise Tax Board assesses a penalty of two hundred fifty dollars ($250). The same $250 penalty applies to corporations and to LLCs, each under its own, separately worded certification statute; if the required statement is filed before the 60-day period expires, or the Secretary of State finds its own delinquency notice was sent in error, the certification — and any penalty already assessed — is withdrawn.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "Upon certification by the Secretary of State pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 2204 or subdivision (a) of Section 17713.09 of the Corporations Code, the Franchise Tax Board shall assess a penalty of two hundred fifty dollars ($250)."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 19141, Penalties and Additions to Tax, the $250 penalty for corporations and LLCs (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=19141.)
  "Upon the failure of a corporation to file the statement required by Section 1502, the Secretary of State shall provide a notice of that delinquency to the corporation. The notice shall also contain information concerning the application of this section, advise the corporation of the penalty imposed by Section 19141 of the Revenue and Taxation Code for failure to timely file the required statement after notice of the delinquency has been provided by the Secretary of State, and shall advise the corporation of its right to request relief from the Secretary of State because of reasonable cause or unusual circumstances that justify the failure to file. If, within 60 days of providing notice of the delinquency, a statement pursuant to Section 1502 has not been filed by the corporation, the Secretary of State shall certify the name of the corporation to the Franchise Tax Board."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 2204(a), Crimes and Penalties, the corporation delinquency-notice and certification procedure (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=2204.)
  "Upon the failure of a limited liability company to file the statement required by Section 17702.09, the Secretary of State shall provide a notice of the delinquency to the limited liability company. The notice shall also contain information concerning the application of this section, advise the limited liability company of the penalty imposed by Section 19141 of the Revenue and Taxation Code for failure to timely file the required statement after notice of delinquency has been mailed by the Secretary of State, and shall advise the limited liability company of its right to request relief from the Secretary of State because of reasonable cause or unusual circumstances that justify such failure to file. If, within 60 days after providing notice of the delinquency, a statement pursuant to Section 17702.09 has not been filed by the limited liability company, the Secretary of State shall certify the name of such limited liability company to the Franchise Tax Board."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17713.09(a), Miscellaneous Provisions, the LLC delinquency-notice and certification procedure (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17713.09.)

This clause cites three different statutory sections: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 19141, which sets the $250 penalty amount and is triggered by certification under either of two Corporations Code provisions; Cal. Corp. Code § 2204(a), the corporation-specific notice-and-certification procedure; and Cal. Corp. Code § 17713.09(a), the separately worded but structurally identical LLC-specific notice-and-certification procedure. These are three independent sources, not subsections of one section. Separately, § 19141 also sets a lower, $50 penalty tied to certification under two other Corporations Code sections (§ 6810 and § 8810), which concern nonprofit mutual benefit and religious corporations; this document does not address nonprofit entities or that $50 penalty, since nonprofit formation is already covered by this project's separate Nonprofit Articles of Incorporation document and was outside this research's scope.

SUSPENSION OF THE ENTITY'S POWERS FOR SUSTAINED NON-FILING
Beyond the $250 penalty, California law provides a separate, more serious consequence for an entity that keeps failing to file. If an entity fails to file its Statement of Information for a given filing period, has not filed one at all during the preceding 24 months, and was already certified to the Franchise Tax Board for the $250 penalty for that same period, the statute switches from a monetary penalty to suspension of the entity's powers: the Secretary of State warns the entity that its powers, rights, and privileges will be suspended in 60 days unless it files, and if the entity still has not filed when that period ends, the Secretary of State notifies the Franchise Tax Board and the entity's powers, rights, and privileges are suspended. Filing the required statement can lift a suspension imposed on this basis, unless the entity is also separately held in suspension by the Franchise Tax Board for unpaid tax, penalty, or interest — a related but legally distinct suspension mechanism, triggered by nonpayment rather than non-filing, under which the same broad phrase — the entity's 'powers, rights, and privileges' — is likewise suspended.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "(a) A corporation that (1) fails to file a statement pursuant to Section 1502 for an applicable filing period, (2) has not filed a statement pursuant to Section 1502 during the preceding 24 months, and (3) was certified for penalty pursuant to Section 2204 for the same filing period, is subject to suspension pursuant to this section rather than to penalty pursuant to Section 2204. (b) When subdivision (a) is applicable, the Secretary of State shall provide a notice to the corporation informing the corporation that its corporate powers, rights, and privileges will be suspended after 60 days if it fails to file a statement pursuant to Section 1502. (c) After the expiration of the 60-day period without any statement filed pursuant to Section 1502, the Secretary of State shall notify the Franchise Tax Board of the suspension and provide a notice of the suspension to the corporation, and thereupon, the corporate powers, rights, and privileges of the corporation are suspended, except for the purpose of filing an application for exempt status or amending the articles of incorporation as necessary either to perfect that application or to set forth a new name."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 2205(a)-(c), Crimes and Penalties, Secretary of State suspension of a corporation for sustained non-filing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=2205.)
  "(a) A limited liability company that (1) fails to file a statement pursuant to Section 17702.09 for an applicable filing period, (2) has not filed a statement pursuant to Section 17702.09 during the preceding 24 months, and (3) was certified for penalty pursuant to Section 17713.09 for the same filing period, shall be subject to suspension pursuant to this section rather than to penalty pursuant to Section 17713.09. (b) When subdivision (a) is applicable, the Secretary of State shall notify the limited liability company that its powers, rights, and privileges will be suspended after 60 days if it fails to file a statement pursuant to Section 17702.09. (c) After the expiration of the 60-day period without any statement filed pursuant to Section 17702.09, the Secretary of State shall notify the Franchise Tax Board of the suspension, and shall provide a notice of the suspension to the limited liability company and thereupon, except for the purpose of amending the articles of organization to set forth a new name, the powers, rights, and privileges of the limited liability company are suspended."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 17713.10(a)-(c), Miscellaneous Provisions, Secretary of State suspension of an LLC for sustained non-filing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17713.10.)
  "Except for the purposes of filing an application for exempt status or amending the articles of incorporation or organization as necessary either to perfect that application or to set forth a new name, the powers, rights, and privileges of a domestic taxpayer may be suspended, and the exercise of the powers, rights, and privileges of a foreign taxpayer in this state may be forfeited, if any of the following conditions occur:"
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23301, Suspension and Revivor, the separate tax-nonpayment suspension mechanism (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=23301.)

(3) The number of vacancies on the board, if any. (4) The names and complete business or residence addresses of its chief executive officer, secretary, and chief financial officer. (5) The street address of its principal executive office. (6) The mailing address of the corporation, if different from the street address of its principal executive office. (7) If the address of its principal executive office is not in this state, the street address of its principal business office in this state, if any. (8) If the corporation chooses to receive renewal notices and any other notifications from the Secretary of State by electronic mail instead of by United States mail, the corporation shall include a valid electronic mail address for the corporation or for the corporation’s designee to receive those notices. (9) A statement of the general type of business that constitutes the principal business activity of the corporation, such as, for example, manufacturer of aircraft, wholesale liquor distributor, or retail department store. (10) A statement indicating whether any officer or any director has an outstanding final judgment issued by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement or a court of law, for which no appeal therefrom is pending, for the violation of any wage order or provision of the Labor Code.

expectedJSON.body: When nothing reported in an entity's most recently filed statement has changed, California does not require the entity to prepare and refile a full new Statement of Information for the next filing period. Instead, both corporations and LLCs may, in lieu of refiling, advise the Secretary of State — on a form the Secretary of State prescribes — that no changes to the previously reported information have occurred during the applicable filing period.

expectedJSON.body: The information below reflects Acme, Inc.'s current records for use in preparing its next Statement of Information filing with the California Secretary of State. Principal office address: 500 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105. Agent for service of process: Jordan Lee, at 500 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105. Current officers and directors (if Acme, Inc. is a corporation) or managers and members (if Acme, Inc. is an LLC): Jordan Lee, CEO; Pat Morgan, Secretary and CFO. General type of business that constitutes Acme, Inc.'s principal business activity: Software as a service for small business accounting. This worksheet organizes the entity's current information for reference. It is not itself the Secretary of State's official statement form, which must be completed and filed in the format the Secretary of State prescribes.

Failing to file a required Statement of Information carries a specific statutory monetary penalty, separate from any Secretary of State filing fee. If a corporation or LLC does not file, the Secretary of State first sends the entity a notice of delinquency describing the penalty and the entity's right to request relief for reasonable cause or unusual circumstances that justify the failure to file. If the required statement still has not been filed 60 days after that notice, the Secretary of State certifies the entity's name to the Franchise Tax Board. Upon that certification, the Franchise Tax Board assesses a penalty of two hundred fifty dollars ($250). The same $250 penalty applies to corporations and to LLCs, each under its own, separately worded certification statute; if the required statement is filed before the 60-day period expires, or the Secretary of State finds its own delinquency notice was sent in error, the certification — and any penalty already assessed — is withdrawn.

citations.quote: Upon certification by the Secretary of State pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 2204 or subdivision (a) of Section 17713.09 of the Corporations Code, the Franchise Tax Board shall assess a penalty of two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

citations.cite: Crimes and Penalties, the corporation delinquency-notice and certification procedure
citations.quote: Upon the failure of a corporation to file the statement required by Section 1502, the Secretary of State shall provide a notice of that delinquency to the corporation. The notice shall also contain information concerning the application of this section, advise the corporation of the penalty imposed by Section 19141 of the Revenue and Taxation Code for failure to timely file the required statement after notice of the delinquency has been provided by the Secretary of State, and shall advise the corporation of its right to request relief from the Secretary of State because of reasonable cause or unusual circumstances that justify the failure to file. If, within 60 days of providing notice of the delinquency, a statement pursuant to Section 1502 has not been filed by the corporation, the Secretary of State shall certify the name of the corporation to the Franchise Tax Board.

The notice shall also contain information concerning the application of this section, advise the limited liability company of the penalty imposed by Section 19141 of the Revenue and Taxation Code for failure to timely file the required statement after notice of delinquency has been mailed by the Secretary of State, and shall advise the limited liability company of its right to request relief from the Secretary of State because of reasonable cause or unusual circumstances that justify such failure to file. If, within 60 days after providing notice of the delinquency, a statement pursuant to Section 17702.09 has not been filed by the limited liability company, the Secretary of State shall certify the name of such limited liability company to the Franchise Tax Board.

expectedJSON.body: Beyond the $250 penalty, California law provides a separate, more serious consequence for an entity that keeps failing to file. If an entity fails to file its Statement of Information for a given filing period, has not filed one at all during the preceding 24 months, and was already certified to the Franchise Tax Board for the $250 penalty for that same period, the statute switches from a monetary penalty to suspension of the entity's powers: the Secretary of State warns the entity that its powers, rights, and privileges will be suspended in 60 days unless it files, and if the entity still has not filed when that period ends, the Secretary of State notifies the Franchise Tax Board and the entity's powers, rights, and privileges are suspended. Filing the required statement can lift a suspension imposed on this basis, unless the entity is also separately held in suspension by the Franchise Tax Board for unpaid tax, penalty, or interest — a related but legally distinct suspension mechanism, triggered by nonpayment rather than non-filing, under which the same broad phrase — the entity's 'powers, rights, and privileges' — is likewise suspended.
